dataset.title: Feather River Beach Seine Fish Survey Data, 1997-2025

abstract.para: This dataset contains fish catch and habitat observations from beach seine surveys of the lower Feather River, California, collected between 1997 and 2025. Surveys were conducted at 42 river-mile sites (225 distinct recorded location names) between river mile 12.5 and 66.5, in both the low flow and high flow channels, to monitor the fish community and the habitat where juvenile fish, particularly juvenile Chinook salmon, were found. [TODO: state who conducted the surveys and the purpose or monitoring program.] Data were compiled from three source periods (1997-2001, 2008-2014 and 2015-2025) and standardized into a single table of 60,699 records from about 2,000 seine samples. Sampling occurred in 1997-2001, 2008-2009, 2013-2014 and 2015-2025; no data are included for 2002-2007 or 2010-2012. Most sampling occurred between January and August. Each record is a fish species (and, from 2008 onward, a count by length) captured in a seine haul, with fork length, life stage, Chinook salmon run and adipose fin clip status where recorded. Each record also carries the sample's water temperature, haul dimensions, depth, substrate, cover, stream feature, gear size and river mile. In total 42 species or taxonomic groups were recorded; Chinook salmon, Sacramento sucker and Sacramento pikeminnow were the most frequently recorded. Observations from 1997-2001 are one row per individual fish, whereas 2008-2025 rows carry a count. Measurement units for haul dimensions and depth differ between source periods and are described in the attribute definitions. These data are published to support the Healthy Rivers and Landscapes Science Program.

description.para: Beach seine surveys were conducted at permanent and alternate sites along the lower Feather River, California, between river mile 12.5 and 66.5. [TODO: describe the sampling design, including how sites were selected, sampling frequency and season, and who conducted the surveys. Link the field sampling protocol or SOP here.]

At each sample, the crew recorded the location name, channel type (side channel, main channel or backwater), bank (river right or river left) and position (upstream, downstream or cross-current), the gear used (beach seine with bag, 10, 25, 39, 50 or 100 feet in length), a condition rating, weather, water temperature, flow, and the dimensions of the haul (haul length, haul width and average depth). Habitat in the sampled area was recorded as the stream feature (riffle, run, glide or pool), all substrate types present and all cover types present. Substrate classes were fine (small gravel, 0-50 mm), small (medium gravel, 50-150 mm), medium (large cobble, 150-300 mm), boulder (greater than 300 mm) and pavement (boat ramp). Cover classes included no apparent cover, small instream objects, large instream objects, overhead objects, submerged aquatic vegetation or algae, and undercut bank. Free-text comments were also recorded.

Captured fish were identified to species, or to the lowest taxonomic group possible for juveniles that could not be identified, and counted. Fork length was measured in millimeters for fish or length classes. Salmonids were assigned a life stage (yolk-sac fry, fry, parr, silvery parr, between parr and smolt, smolt or adult) and Chinook salmon were assigned a run (fall, spring, late fall, winter or unknown); the field datasheet lists length-at-date criteria for each run. Fish with a clipped adipose fin were recorded. From 2015 onward, fish weight was also recorded for some fish.

Data were compiled from three sources: a spreadsheet of individual fish captured in 1997-2001, a spreadsheet of seine data for 2008-2014, and an Access database for 2015-2025. Observations in 1997-2001 are one row per individual fish; later periods record a count for each species and length. Data for 2002-2007 and 2010-2012 are not included.

Units for haul dimensions, depth and distance out differ between the 1997-2001 data (apparently feet) and the 2008-2025 data (apparently meters) and have not been harmonized; see the attribute definitions. Sample IDs are not unique across source periods; a sample can be identified by date, location and sample ID together. Haul width is largely missing for 2015-2025, so haul area is not available for most of that period. dataTable.entityName: Beach Seine Catch and Habitat Observations
dataTable.entityDescription: Fish catch (species, count, fork length, life stage) and associated sample habitat and water quality measurements for beach seine hauls on the lower Feather River. Each row is one species/length record from a seine haul; sample-level measurements are repeated across rows of the same sample.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Date the seine sample was collected.

Identifier of the seine sample (one seine survey at one location on one date). From the source database sample ID for 2008-2025 and the source seine ID for 1997-2001. REVIEW: IDs are not unique across source periods (399 values are reused), so identify a sample by date + location + sample_id.

textDomain.definition: Identifier of the seine sample (one seine survey at one location on one date). From the source database sample ID for 2008-2025 and the source seine ID for 1997-2001. REVIEW: IDs are not unique across source periods (399 values are reused), so identify a sample by date + location + sample_id.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Name of the sampling location as recorded in the source data. Raw names are kept (spelling and format vary by source period and include side-channel, bank and upstream/downstream qualifiers); use river_mile to group locations by site.

textDomain.definition: Name of the sampling location as recorded in the source data. Raw names are kept (spelling and format vary by source period and include side-channel, bank and upstream/downstream qualifiers); use river_mile to group locations by site.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Feather River channel the location is in: HFC (High Flow Channel), LFC (Low Flow Channel), or 'HFC DS LYR'. REVIEW: confirm the meaning of 'HFC DS LYR' (likely downstream of the Yuba River confluence). Not recorded for 1997-2014 data or a small number of 2015-2025 records.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Sampling gear type. All records are beach seine (SEIN); other gear types in the source data (nets, electrofishing) were removed.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Water temperature at the time of sampling. 1997-2001 values were recorded in degrees Fahrenheit and converted to Celsius (a recorded value of 0 was treated as not recorded); a single entry of 147 for sample 1628 was corrected to 17 per the data owner.

Secchi depth, recorded in 1997-2001 data only (source column 'sechi'). REVIEW: about 99% of values are 0, which likely means not recorded, and units are not documented - confirm units or remove this column.

Common name of the fish species (lower case) as standardized from source codes and spellings. Includes unidentified groups (e.g. unidentified juvenile minnow) and the composite 'sacramento pikeminnow or hardhead'. Chinook salmon and O. mykiss are not split by race or origin here; see run and adipose_clipped. Blank where no fish were caught.

missingValueCode.codeExplanation: No fish caught or species not recorded

attribute.attributeDefinition: Fork length of the fish (1997-2001: individual fish; 2008-2025: length of the fish or length class counted in count), in millimeters. Blank where fish were counted but not measured (a recorded length of 0 was set to missing).

Life stage of salmonids recorded by the crew: yolk-sac fry, fry, parr, silvery parr, between parr and smolt, smolt, or adult; 'n/p' as entered in the source data (assumed 'not provided'). Recorded for salmonids only.

textDomain.definition: Life stage of salmonids recorded by the crew: yolk-sac fry, fry, parr, silvery parr, between parr and smolt, smolt, or adult; 'n/p' as entered in the source data (assumed 'not provided'). Recorded for salmonids only.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Chinook salmon run (Fall, Spring, Late Fall, Winter or Unknown), taken from the species entry in the source data. Blank for all non-Chinook records.

textDomain.definition: Chinook salmon run (Fall, Spring, Late Fall, Winter or Unknown), taken from the species entry in the source data. Blank for all non-Chinook records.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Length of the seine haul. REVIEW (units differ by source period): 1997-2001 values appear to be in feet (e.g. round values such as 35 and 15 for a 39 ft seine), 2008-2025 values appear to be in meters (e.g. 4.572 = 15 ft). Not yet harmonized in the clean data - confirm with data owner. Source columns: 'length' (1997-2001) and 'bs_start_length' (2008-2025).

Width of the seine haul at close of the haul. REVIEW (units differ by source period): 1997-2001 values appear to be in feet (e.g. round values such as 35 and 15 for a 39 ft seine), 2008-2025 values appear to be in meters (e.g. 4.572 = 15 ft). Not yet harmonized in the clean data - confirm with data owner. Source column 'bs_close_width' (2008-2025). REVIEW: 2015-2025 values are 0 to 0.6 and about 98% are missing, which does not look like a haul width.

Distance from the bank that the seine was deployed. REVIEW (units differ by source period): 1997-2001 values appear to be in feet (e.g. round values such as 35 and 15 for a 39 ft seine), 2008-2025 values appear to be in meters (e.g. 4.572 = 15 ft). Not yet harmonized in the clean data - confirm with data owner. REVIEW: confirm the exact definition.
Water depth at the haul point farthest from shore ('full distance out'), recorded in 1997-2001 data only. REVIEW: depth units are probably feet for this period - confirm.
Water depth at the haul point closest to shore, recorded in 1997-2001 data only. REVIEW: depth units are probably feet for this period - confirm.
Stream feature (mesohabitat unit) of the sampled area: Riffle, Run, Glide or Pool, or a combination joined with '&' where more than one was recorded.

textDomain.definition: Stream feature (mesohabitat unit) of the sampled area: Riffle, Run, Glide or Pool, or a combination joined with '&' where more than one was recorded.

attribute.attributeDefinition: Area of the sampled haul. REVIEW (inconsistent between periods): 1997-2001 values are supplied in the source data and equal haul length x width; 2008-2025 values were calculated as length x width x average depth, which is a volume. Only 43 values exist for 2015-2025 and all are 0 because width is mostly missing. Confirm the definition and units before publishing.
Number of fish of this species (and length, where measured) in the record. Blank for 1997-2001 data, where each row is one individual fish.

missingValueCode.codeExplanation: Not recorded (1997-2001 rows are individual fish)

attribute.attributeDefinition: Average water depth of the haul. REVIEW (units differ by source period): 1997-2001 values appear to be in feet (e.g. round values such as 35 and 15 for a 39 ft seine), 2008-2025 values appear to be in meters (e.g. 4.572 = 15 ft). Not yet harmonized in the clean data - confirm with data owner. Source column 'bs_depth_1_2', confirmed by the data owner to be the average depth. Two entries missing a decimal point (samples 899 and 1066) were corrected.

missingValueCode.codeExplanation: Not recorded (1997-2001 data) or not entered

attribute.attributeDefinition: Weight of the fish, in grams. Recorded in 2015-2025 data only.
Calendar year of the sample, derived from date.

River mile of the standardized river-mile site assigned to the sampling location, measured in miles upstream from the Feather River's confluence with the Sacramento River (REVIEW: confirm RM 0 definition). Locations were assigned to a site using the program's Subsite Table, supplemented by manual assignments.
Number of seine hauls (pulls) made in the sample, parsed from free-text crew comments (e.g. '2 pulls'). Blank when no count was stated in the comments, which does not imply a single haul.

Substrate types present in the sampled area, as comma-separated categories: Fine (small gravel, 0-50 mm), Small (medium gravel, 50-150 mm), Medium (large cobble, 150-300 mm), Boulder (>300 mm) or Pavement (boat ramp). All substrate present is recorded; the order listed does not indicate dominance.
